lead.headline: Outside evaluator says Anthropic is speeding up its own AI development more than it admitted
lead.summary: METR, an independent evaluator, reviewed Anthropic's internal evidence from August to October and concluded the company's public risk report understated how much AI is accelerating its research. METR estimates capability gains on well-specified tasks are running at roughly twice the earlier pace, while stressing the uncertainty and that Anthropic redacted much of the key evidence.

stories.headline: Why identical deep-learning training runs can end up in different places
stories.summary: Published in Nature Machine Intelligence, this University of Sydney work argues that fractal 'riddled basin' geometry in training makes outcomes inherently hard to predict or reproduce, even with extremely precise starting conditions. It is drawing attention because it challenges the habit of blaming randomness alone for run-to-run differences in AI models.

stories.headline: AI-native autonomous lab coordinates 20+ instruments for multi-objective experiments
stories.summary: Reported as newly published in Nature, the AutoDNA system from Shanghai Jiao Tong University uses multiple AI agents to run biomolecular experiments across many instrument types with little human input. The journal listing was confirmed only through secondary reporting, and an earlier preprint of the work exists.

stories.headline: METR: Anthropic's own AI is speeding up its research
stories.summary: METR's report says its high-access review found the public risk report understated acceleration, and Anthropic says it will publish its own analysis in coming weeks.

stories.headline: Mistral releases weights for its roughly 1-trillion-parameter Large 4
stories.summary: The French lab has made its biggest open-weight model downloadable, under a modified MIT-style licence. Performance claims are Mistral's own and not independently verified.

stories.headline: Big Build royal commission hears CFMEU influence was 'unprecedented'
stories.summary: The first day of a two-week hearing block heard a major contractor worry about the union's access to ministers in the Andrews government.

stories.headline: Calls for next Victorian government to invest in prisons
stories.summary: With the state election weeks away, advocates are pressing whichever party wins to fund the prison system.

stories.headline: Police fear for teen missing near Walhalla
stories.summary: A 17-year-old left his camp in the Alpine region four days ago and is still missing, with snow on nearby mountains raising concern.

stories.headline: Khawaja says Victoria was best at ball tampering in Shield cricket
stories.summary: Usman Khawaja made a pointed claim about Victoria's past conduct in Sheffield Shield cricket.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco tower in Riyadh damaged in attempted attack
stories.summary: A tower in Riyadh's financial district was reported damaged as a coalition said it intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at the capital and the Eastern Province.

thought: Small steps, taken daily, are still the whole journey.
